subject.title: fix: show readable session names across Windows UX

question: Should Windows hide Gateway-classified background sessions by default across the composer, tray menu, dashboard, and Sessions page while adopting the coordinated presentation contract?
rationale: The branch deliberately changes which existing sessions remain discoverable after upgrade, and automated review cannot decide whether that cross-surface visibility policy matches intended Windows UX or whether it should be separated from the title fix.

options.title: Approve staged landing
options.body: Confirm the Gateway contract and background-session policy, collect native current-head proof, then land the coordinated change with the existing compatibility coverage.

options.title: Split title and visibility work
options.body: Land readable presentation metadata and raw-key preservation first, while moving default background filtering into a narrower follow-up with separate UX review.

options.title: Preserve current visibility
options.body: Keep all existing sessions visible by default and make background filtering an explicit opt-in preference on each affected surface.

recommendation.title: Approve staged landing
recommendation.body: Confirm the Gateway contract and background-session policy, collect native current-head proof, then land the coordinated change with the existing compatibility coverage.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision spans established Windows tray behavior, Gateway compatibility, and upgrade-visible UX across several core surfaces.
